bullets.title: NVDA CEO Jensen Huang facing imminent removal — 8+ downgrades, stock -8% premarket
bullets.body: Nvidia's board is reportedly preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang following reports of an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative and an internal investigation via Wachtell Lipton. The stock is down ~8% premarket with Polymarket pricing ~68% odds of removal by Nov 30. At least 8 sell-side downgrades overnight (Melius to hold/$185, Evercore to in-line/$186, Bernstein to market perform/$200, Baird to neutral/$200, Oppenheimer to perform, William Blair to market perform, KeyBanc to sector weight, Aletheia to hold), with PT cuts to $180–$230 range; prior PTs clustered around $315–$500.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO departure: key risks are financing pause, export controls, and succession — not near-term fundamentals
bullets.body: Analysts broadly agree NVDA's AI demand fundamentals (FQ3 ~$113B revenue, FQ4 guide ~$129B vs $124B street) are unaffected through CY28, but the bear case centers on three concerns: (1) Huang's $50B+ quarterly AI ecosystem financing could pause under new leadership, (2) ~20% of revenue exposed to Singapore/Southeast Asia routes at risk from tighter export controls, and (3) no obvious internal successor — Colette Kress (CFO) flagged as interim, Ian Buck as internal candidate. Wolfe argues CEO discount may already be priced at under 8x FY29 EPS; Piper sees $150 floor at 10x trough CY27 EPS.

bullets.title: Semi complex broadly lower; AMD and AVGO bid as NVDA rotation plays
bullets.body: The semiconductor complex is trading down in sympathy — MU -5.4%, STX -4.9%, SMCI -6.7%, SMH -2.5% premarket — while AMD and AVGO are bid higher as perceived beneficiaries of NVDA share and capital rotation. William Blair simultaneously upgraded AMD to outperform. Oppenheimer, Klein, RBC, and Citi all flag AMD/AVGO/MRVL/TSM as the cleaner names to own for AI/semi beta through the NVDA governance overhang.

bullets.title: Export controls tightening: Commerce advancing rule blocking Chinese AI firms' remote chip access
bullets.body: The Commerce Department is finalizing a rule to prevent Chinese AI firms from remotely accessing advanced chips abroad (targeting Southeast Asian data center workarounds). Chinese AI firms are rushing to lock in overseas Nvidia capacity in anticipation. Separately, the DoJ received a transferred investigation into alleged chip smuggling via Megaspeed International (~$5B+ NVDA sales), and the White House is considering new export controls on advanced AI chips — timing accelerated by the Huang scandal's geopolitical implications ahead of the Trump-Xi summit.

bullets.title: AI capex outlook robust despite NVDA noise: GS models $1.4tn annualized run-rate by end-2027
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs forecasts AI capex exceeding $900B annualized by end-2026 and reaching $1.4tn by end-2027, implying 8% real business fixed investment growth Q4/Q4 2027 vs consensus 4.2%. Every $100B of AI capex = ~$9 SPX EPS (~2.5% earnings growth) in 2027 per JPM. Hyperscalers (AMZN, MSFT, META, GOOGL) are expected to absorb chips redirected from Southeast Asia if export restrictions tighten.

bullets.title: AI enterprise spend growth collapsing: OpenAI/Anthropic growth slowing sharply, token prices -15%
bullets.body: AI enterprise spending growth has collapsed from double-digit monthly rates to under 2% in October per Market Voices analysis. Average token prices fell nearly 15% in October; OpenAI and Anthropic revenue growth slowed to 2.1% and 0.5% respectively. Top 1% of businesses drive 80% of OpenAI/Anthropic spending, making the ecosystem vulnerable to VC funding headwinds. Anthropic's IPO valuation may be falling from $2T toward ~$1.3T, though separately Wolfe notes the IPO is multiple times oversubscribed at ~$90B.

bullets.title: Futures modestly lower; 10-year yield back at 5%; NVDA overhang weighing on AI trade
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures are down ~0.4–0.5% and Nasdaq 100 futures down ~1% as of early Thursday morning, with the 10-year yield ticking back to 4.99–5.01%. The AI momentum index opened +50bps Wednesday but closed -1%, suggesting limited retail chasing. JPM notes levered ETF selling of ~$95B over two days with CTAs flipped net short and ~$50B more to sell; they remain tactically bullish targeting SPX 8,000 YE26 (21.9x 365 EPS, ~8.4% upside from close).

bullets.title: Macro: Inflation broadening; productivity gains insufficient to offset inflationary policy mix
bullets.body: PSC Macro flags that productivity growth over the past three years cannot contain inflation given accelerating M2 growth and rising government spending. Rising labor demand hitting limited supply creates wage inflation risk for 2027, with 'hotter' CPI components outpacing 'cooler' ones. Separately, GS models 8% real business fixed investment growth in 2027 vs 4.2% consensus, partly driven by AI capex.

bullets.title: CRWV raises $4B investment-grade debt; contract economics expanding materially
bullets.body: CoreWeave is raising at least $4B in high-grade loans at 7–7.5% yield (investment-grade vs prior junk-bond status). Contract-level TCV/CapEx has expanded to 2.5–2.75x for 5-year contracts vs 2.0x end-2025, with levered IRRs well above 30% hurdle. Hopper GPU renewals are pricing 25–50% above original contracted levels. Microsoft's share of backlog has declined to <10% from ~85% at IPO; >50% of new customers this year are from outside AI/tech.

bullets.title: NBIS Q3 massive beat: $6.4B ARR (+1,062% YoY), adj. EBITDA margin 47.5%, capex fully prepaid
bullets.body: Nebius reported Q3 revenue of $980.8M (+8% beat), adj. EBITDA of $465.8M (+32% beat vs $351.8M consensus), and ARR of $6.4B vs $4.7B expected. Gross margin hit 77.6% vs 71.3% forecast. Customer prepayments now cover >100% of associated capex (ex <1-year deals), up from 50–60% in Q2. 2027 revenue guidance of $12–13B with capex of $40–45B was well above $29B street estimate; stock had been up 26.8% since Aug 11 prior to print.

bullets.title: UK GDP 3Q beats at +3% annualized; 4Q revised up but energy bills threaten 1Q27
bullets.body: UK Q3 GDP rose 0.7% Q/Q (3% annualized) on strong domestic demand and 0.6% consumption growth. JPM raised its 4Q forecast to 1.5% annualized but cut 1Q27 to 1.0% on anticipated sharp energy bill increases expected to drive ~5% annualized CPI. AI contribution to UK GDP has moderated to 0.1–0.2% annualized vs prior 0.3% claims after a sharp drop in computer programming activity in September.

bullets.title: Euro area labor market lagging growth; two-speed economy with Germany shedding jobs
bullets.body: Euro area employment growth was near zero in 3Q26 despite 1% GDP expansion, with JPM cutting its 2H26 employment forecast to 0.2% annualized from 0.5%. Germany and France are losing jobs while periphery countries remain resilient; German firms appear to be taking productivity gains rather than hiring. Recovery to 0.3% employment growth in 4Q is expected only if core labor demand improves.

bullets.title: Semis AI cycle: multiples compressed 35% since May; JPM sees tech washout near completion
bullets.body: AI company multiples have compressed ~35% since May (Semis -52%, Memory -60%), with the software index (IGV) returning -9.5% YTD vs S&P +10.5%. JPM sees the tech washout as near completion and flags US Memory and Semis via options as near-term opportunities. Separately, RBC notes AI winners (semis, networking, optical) have been outperforming while hyperscalers underperform.

bullets.title: GOOGL: 'Hydrogen' model in internal testing; EU AdSense fine revived by court adviser
bullets.body: Google is internally testing a new Gemini model codenamed 'Hydrogen' designed for speed and efficiency — viewed as a modest positive for broader AI use cases and agentic applications. Separately, an EU court adviser recommended revisiting the lower court annulment of a €1.5B AdSense fine, adding regulatory overhang to GOOGL.

bullets.title: HUBS +7.4% premarket on CEO Rangan stepping down; co-founder Halligan returns
bullets.body: HubSpot CEO Yamini Rangan is stepping down effective November 12; co-founder Brian Halligan is returning as CEO. CFO Kate Bueker will retire February 11, replaced by Karen Burgess from Adobe. The company reaffirmed Q4 and full-year 2026 guidance. Stock is up ~7.4% premarket.

bullets.title: Hedgeye turns tactically bearish: shorting QQQ and NVDA, targeting VXN 38 and SPX 7313 support
bullets.body: Hedgeye sees an AI bubble imploding, flagging 339M NVDA shares traded on the 'consensus bottom' call as bubble behavior. They are selling QQQ on momentum exhaustion, adding a copper short on AI implosion thesis, and targeting VXN near 38. SPX immediate-term support seen at 7,313 with 10-year yield range 4.81–5.02%.

bullets.title: AI capex read-through: TLN wins 750MW Guernsey data center contract; GEV gas turbine orders +43% YoY
bullets.body: Talen Energy raised 2028 FCF/share guidance to $48 base/$53 with buybacks after securing a new 750MW Guernsey power contract for 2029/30 generating ~$100M annually; GS raised PT to $502. GE Vernova's gas-turbine capacity share rose to 41.6% from 31% in 2025 on 93.8GW orders (+43% YoY through 9M26), with US electricity output up 325TWh vs three years ago — the largest increase since 2003.

bullets.title: Xi-Trump summit next week complicated by NVDA spy scandal; trade ceasefire expires in <2 months
bullets.body: The NVDA CEO scandal is adding geopolitical complexity ahead of a Trump-Xi summit next week. China's Foreign Ministry denied using the espionage allegations as a pretext for tech restrictions. With the US-China trade ceasefire expiring in under two months, the scandal is accelerating Washington's push for tighter AI chip export controls and complicating bilateral negotiations.
